name: Mince Pies (No. 1)
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: currants, washed, picked over, and dried
ingredients.originalText: 2 lbs. currants, washed, picked over, and dried

ingredients.name: brown sugar to make very sweet
ingredients.originalText: brown sugar to make very sweet

instructions.text: The meat should be a good piece of lean beef, boiled the day before it is needed.
Half a pound of raw suet, chopped fine, may be added.
Chop the meat, clean out bits of skin and gristle, and mix with twice the quantity of fine juicy apples, also chopped.
Then put in the fruit, next the sugar and spice, lastly the liquor.
Mix very thoroughly, cover closely, and let all stand together for twenty-four hours before making the pies.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. The meat should be a good piece of lean beef, boiled the day before it is needed.
2. Half a pound of raw suet, chopped fine, may be added.
3. Chop the meat, clean out bits of skin and gristle, and mix with twice the quantity of fine juicy apples, also chopped.
4. Then put in the fruit, next the sugar and spice, lastly the liquor.
5. Mix very thoroughly, cover closely, and let all stand together for twenty-four hours before making the pies.
